source_question.title: Why am I getting a foreign key mismatch when trying to join 2 tables using foreign keys?
source_question.body:
I am doing Chapter 16 - SQLite Databases of Automate the Boring Stuff with Python By Al. Sweigart and I ran into a problem in the "Joining Multiple Tables with Foreign Keys" part, let it be known that I just started to get into python and I am for the first time learning about databases and SQLite.

I have a file called sweigartcats.db containing a table called "cats", these are its columns:

>>> conn.execute('PRAGMA TABLE_INFO(cats)').fetchall()
[(0, 'name', 'TEXT', 1, None, 0), (1, 'birthdate', 'TEXT', 0, None, 0), (2, 'fur', 'TEXT', 0, None, 0), (3, 'weight_kg', 'REAL', 0, None, 0)]

The tutorial is showing how to create another table called vaccinations (which is successfully created) with the following structure:

>>> conn.execute('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vaccinations (vaccine TEXT,
date_administered TEXT, administered_by TEXT, cat_id INTEGER,
FOREIGN KEY(cat_id) REFERENCES cats(rowid)) STRICT')

The values inserted into the vaccinations table use the rowid of the cats table to connect vaccination data to a selected cat, in this case the cat "Zophie" has the rowid of 1:

>>> conn.execute('INSERT INTO vaccinations VALUES ("rabies", "2023-06-06", "Dr. Echo", 1)')

However, instead of returning a Cursor object, it gives me an error:

sqlite3.OperationalError: foreign key mismatch - "vaccinations" referencing "cats"

Earlier today for whatever reason that error didn't happen when I inserted the values (I don't remember doing anything different) and I managed to use the following code to return a tuple that joined the rowid cat and its vaccines data:

>>> conn.execute('SELECT * FROM cats INNER JOIN vaccinations ON cats.rowid = 
vaccinations.cat_id').fetchall()

But that didn't last as the foreign key mismatch error happened right next to it when i tried to use iterdumps() to copy the database to a .txt file, I tried redoing it using the original file many times but the error always happens and I can no longer insert anything into the vaccinations table (even if i copy the code straight from the website to make sure it's not a typo).

I'm not sure if it's needed but here are the queries used to create the original file: https://pastebin.com/neG0q4Ai

I checked the sqlite3 docs and some questions here and apparently there might be an issue with using rowid as a foreign key, but I'm not very familiar with it so I can't be sure, also the fact that it is in the book with no regards to any errors and I couldn't find anyone else with the same error in this specific lesson could mean I am getting something wrong.

One of the practice programs at the end of that chapter involves checking the vaccinations of the cats so I can only do it if I can make this work first.

I apologize if I forgot to add an important piece of information and I'll add it if needed.
